documents.title: Guidelines for the Use of Generative Artificial Intelligence (GenAI) Tools at UMD
documents.stance_why: The guidelines say 'It will be at the course instructor's discretion to determine whether GenAI may be used, to what extent, and for which assignments', and give students a fallback ('should assume ... not allowed unless otherwise specified'). They set no single rule, and name three options (permitted, permitted with acknowledgment, not permitted), so the decision is handed to instructors.
documents.summary: Approved January 2025 guidelines covering teaching, research and administrative use. For courses, instructors decide and students assume AI is not allowed unless the syllabus says so. The text also sets rules on data levels, approved tools such as TerpAI, detectors, and reporting.

notes: Consensus of coders A and B. Course layer deferred in the collect file. The UMD guidelines page repeats the FAQ and summary text from the policy itself; only the summary lines that add information (instructor options, syllabus check) were coded separately. CS page stance coded prohibit because the AI item has no permission qualifier, but the page also defers to each syllabus; a reader could code it restrict. Two UNCOVERED units: personal liability for click-through terms, and UMD's right to review prompts and outputs. | Coder B: Coder B. The CS page says to read the syllabus for what is permissible but lists AI use for class work as a violation applying to all courses; coded prohibit. Non-AI integrity items on the CS page (hardcoding, code sharing, similarity software) were not coded. Repeated sample-syllabus sentences in the TLTC page (email for exceptions, cite per assignment directions) were coded once.
